/**
 * Week 3 — work, study and the wider world.
 *
 * Longer words, unstressed syllables, and the doubling that happens (or does
 * not) when a suffix arrives. This is where the two rules from week 1 stop
 * being separate exercises and start colliding: `hoping` and `hopping` differ
 * by one letter and one rule, and the pair is in here on purpose, as are
 * `writing`/`written`, `desert`/`dessert` and the -ise verbs whose ending a
 * learner has probably seen spelled both ways.
 *
 * The irregular plurals arrive here too — children, women, feet, teeth, mice,
 * knives, leaves — because a learner who has just been taught -s and -es needs
 * the exceptions before they over-apply the rule to everything.
 */

days.title: Work and money
days.focus: The -ment nouns, and the vocabulary of a job, a salary and a budget.

days.title: Machines and science
days.focus: Longer words with unstressed syllables, and the -cience/-cient family.

days.title: Study and the city
days.focus: University, library, dictionary — the -ary and -ory endings that sound alike.

days.title: Land, weather and animals
days.focus: The natural world, and desert against dessert.

days.title: Hoping and hopping
days.focus: The two rules colliding: one letter, one doubling, two different words.

days.title: Plurals that break the rule
days.focus: Children, women, feet, teeth, knives, leaves — before over-applying -s.

days.title: Character and choice
days.focus: The -ous and -ive adjectives, and the -ise verbs learners see spelled both ways.
